# Sonar exceptions — JPWB

<!-- Generated from docs/operations/sonar-exceptions.json by `bun run sonar:exceptions`; do not edit by hand. -->

The Sonar findings JPWB leaves in place on purpose, each under JAN-ENGC-001 §7.4 and approved by a register ruling that names it. The procedure is `docs/operations/sonarqube.md` §8. The source is `docs/operations/sonar-exceptions.json`; `verif/sonar-exceptions.test.ts` joins it with the markers in the Sonar scope and checks this page against it.

At a site, a finding left in place carries the marker `// eslint-disable-next-line <rule> -- EXC-nnn <reason>`. No other ESLint directive that can turn a rule off is admitted in the Sonar scope, and no comment may start with NOSONAR.

## Exceptions

No exception is recorded.

A finding in these folders cannot take a marker without re-pinning the test, so its entry is `pinned`: located by path, rule and count, and held by the engine baseline (route (b)).

## The 15 rule names the plugin shares with ESLint core or typescript-eslint

The rule names eslint-plugin-sonarjs shares with ESLint core or typescript-eslint, derived from the packages' own metadata: each plugin rule folder's eslintId and sonarKey, against ESLint's built-in rules and typescript-eslint's plugin rules. The engine matches a marker by its rule name's last segment, so a marker naming the shared rule may also silence the Sonar rule (DESIGN-sonar-configuration-management.md F-5, D-5).
